method: PARAPHRASED AND HASH-ANCHORED from American Society of Hematology (ASH) guideline panel (DuVall AS, et al.), Blood Advances 'American Society of Hematology 2026 guidelines for frontline management of acute lymphoblastic leukemia in adolescents and young adults' (published 4 July 2026). Every claim is a paraphrase backed by anchors (scripts/anchor.py): verify.py --source re-finds each anchored span in a fresh copy of the source, checks the claim's numbers against it and rejects copying. LICENCE: CC BY-NC-ND 4.0 (read at Europe PMC fullTextXML <license> element for PMC13366240). The source's words are NOT reproduced here.

claims.claim: **The source covers adolescents and young adults (AYAs), aged 15 to 39 at diagnosis.** The panel notes that data for the whole band were limited, particularly for the youngest patients.
claims.locator: American Society of Hematology (ASH) guideline panel (DuVall AS, et al.), Blood Advances, 'American Society of Hematology 2026 guidelines for frontline management of acute lymphoblastic leukemia in adolescents and young adults', published 4 July 2026, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC13366240/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Treat AYAs with B-ALL, T-ALL or T-lymphoblastic lymphoma using a paediatric-style regimen built on asparaginase.** (Strong; moderate certainty)
claims.locator: American Society of Hematology (ASH) guideline panel (DuVall AS, et al.), Blood Advances, 'American Society of Hematology 2026 guidelines for frontline management of acute lymphoblastic leukemia in adolescents and young adults', published 4 July 2026, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC13366240/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Allogeneic transplant is not suggested as routine consolidation in first remission** (conditional). It may still benefit high-risk groups, such as those with persistent MRD, induction failure or adverse biology.
claims.locator: American Society of Hematology (ASH) guideline panel (DuVall AS, et al.), Blood Advances, 'American Society of Hematology 2026 guidelines for frontline management of acute lymphoblastic leukemia in adolescents and young adults', published 4 July 2026, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC13366240/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Pegaspargase can be capped or reduced to limit toxicity** without apparent harm to disease control (conditional). A cap means no more than 3750 IU per dose. Reduction means under 2500 IU/m2 before age 22, or under 2000 IU/m2 from age 22.
claims.locator: American Society of Hematology (ASH) guideline panel (DuVall AS, et al.), Blood Advances, 'American Society of Hematology 2026 guidelines for frontline management of acute lymphoblastic leukemia in adolescents and young adults', published 4 July 2026, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC13366240/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Premedicate before asparaginase**, with at least an IV corticosteroid, optionally adding an antihistamine or paracetamol (strong). When doses are capped or reduced, or premedication is used, check asparaginase activity. Aim for ≥0.1 IU/mL maintained for 14 days or longer.
claims.locator: American Society of Hematology (ASH) guideline panel (DuVall AS, et al.), Blood Advances, 'American Society of Hematology 2026 guidelines for frontline management of acute lymphoblastic leukemia in adolescents and young adults', published 4 July 2026, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC13366240/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Do not give cryoprecipitate or fibrinogen concentrate routinely unless there is bleeding, and do not use unfractionated heparin as routine thromboprophylaxis** (both strong). The evidence cannot settle routine LMWH or DOAC prophylaxis either way.
claims.locator: American Society of Hematology (ASH) guideline panel (DuVall AS, et al.), Blood Advances, 'American Society of Hematology 2026 guidelines for frontline management of acute lymphoblastic leukemia in adolescents and young adults', published 4 July 2026, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC13366240/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **After an allergic reaction to pegaspargase, change to an Erwinia-derived asparaginase** rather than dropping asparaginase altogether. (Strong)
claims.locator: American Society of Hematology (ASH) guideline panel (DuVall AS, et al.), Blood Advances, 'American Society of Hematology 2026 guidelines for frontline management of acute lymphoblastic leukemia in adolescents and young adults', published 4 July 2026, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC13366240/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **For CD20-positive B-ALL, add rituximab to chemotherapy** (conditional). Its dose, timing, schedule and the CD20 threshold remain uncertain.
claims.locator: American Society of Hematology (ASH) guideline panel (DuVall AS, et al.), Blood Advances, 'American Society of Hematology 2026 guidelines for frontline management of acute lymphoblastic leukemia in adolescents and young adults', published 4 July 2026, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC13366240/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Once B-ALL is in morphological remission, add blinatumomab, whatever the MRD result.** (Conditional; very low certainty)
claims.locator: American Society of Hematology (ASH) guideline panel (DuVall AS, et al.), Blood Advances, 'American Society of Hematology 2026 guidelines for frontline management of acute lymphoblastic leukemia in adolescents and young adults', published 4 July 2026, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC13366240/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Blinatumomab carries real toxicity and burden.** In the trial, grade ≥3 neurological events were the only significant excess harm. Cytokine release syndrome, infusion reactions and hypogammaglobulinaemia also occur. It is started in hospital and given as 28-day continuous infusions.
claims.locator: American Society of Hematology (ASH) guideline panel (DuVall AS, et al.), Blood Advances, 'American Society of Hematology 2026 guidelines for frontline management of acute lymphoblastic leukemia in adolescents and young adults', published 4 July 2026, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC13366240/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Inotuzumab has no frontline recommendation** because the evidence was insufficient.
claims.locator: American Society of Hematology (ASH) guideline panel (DuVall AS, et al.), Blood Advances, 'American Society of Hematology 2026 guidelines for frontline management of acute lymphoblastic leukemia in adolescents and young adults', published 4 July 2026, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC13366240/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **T-cell disease:** nelarabine is not suggested for T-lymphoblastic lymphoma, and bortezomib is not suggested for T-ALL. (Both conditional)
claims.locator: American Society of Hematology (ASH) guideline panel (DuVall AS, et al.), Blood Advances, 'American Society of Hematology 2026 guidelines for frontline management of acute lymphoblastic leukemia in adolescents and young adults', published 4 July 2026, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC13366240/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Ph-positive ALL: induce with reduced-intensity therapy plus a TKI** in preference to intensive chemotherapy plus a TKI (conditional). Post-remission treatment follows, with intensive chemotherapy and/or immunotherapy, each with a TKI. Transplant in first remission can consolidate either route.
claims.locator: American Society of Hematology (ASH) guideline panel (DuVall AS, et al.), Blood Advances, 'American Society of Hematology 2026 guidelines for frontline management of acute lymphoblastic leukemia in adolescents and young adults', published 4 July 2026, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC13366240/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **The reason is fewer early deaths:** death within 60 days was lower with reduced-intensity induction plus a TKI (RR 0.25; 95% CI 0.07-0.85).
claims.locator: American Society of Hematology (ASH) guideline panel (DuVall AS, et al.), Blood Advances, 'American Society of Hematology 2026 guidelines for frontline management of acute lymphoblastic leukemia in adolescents and young adults', published 4 July 2026, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC13366240/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **The guideline does not choose a TKI.** Most comparative data came from imatinib. Only one retrospective study included some dasatinib or nilotinib use, and ponatinib-based results were not yet available.
claims.locator: American Society of Hematology (ASH) guideline panel (DuVall AS, et al.), Blood Advances, 'American Society of Hematology 2026 guidelines for frontline management of acute lymphoblastic leukemia in adolescents and young adults', published 4 July 2026, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC13366240/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Give CNS prophylaxis as intrathecal methotrexate or triple intrathecal therapy, either being acceptable** (conditional). Every Ph-positive patient must receive concurrent intrathecal prophylaxis. Cranial irradiation is not suggested routinely on a paediatric-style backbone (conditional).
claims.locator: American Society of Hematology (ASH) guideline panel (DuVall AS, et al.), Blood Advances, 'American Society of Hematology 2026 guidelines for frontline management of acute lymphoblastic leukemia in adolescents and young adults', published 4 July 2026, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC13366240/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **MRD measurement is standard care.** It carries prognostic weight and sometimes sets treatment intensity. Most studies call MRD positive at ≥0.01% by quantitative flow or clone-specific methods.
claims.locator: American Society of Hematology (ASH) guideline panel (DuVall AS, et al.), Blood Advances, 'American Society of Hematology 2026 guidelines for frontline management of acute lymphoblastic leukemia in adolescents and young adults', published 4 July 2026, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC13366240/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **If MRD persists after 3 months or more of frontline treatment** (induction and at least 1 post-remission block), **change the approach** (strong). Immunotherapy or allogeneic transplant are options; their best timing, selection and order are undefined.
claims.locator: American Society of Hematology (ASH) guideline panel (DuVall AS, et al.), Blood Advances, 'American Society of Hematology 2026 guidelines for frontline management of acute lymphoblastic leukemia in adolescents and young adults', published 4 July 2026, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC13366240/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **AYA-specific care (good practice):** arrange fertility consultation before treatment starts where possible. Screen routinely for depression and anxiety, and provide multidisciplinary psychosocial support.
claims.locator: American Society of Hematology (ASH) guideline panel (DuVall AS, et al.), Blood Advances, 'American Society of Hematology 2026 guidelines for frontline management of acute lymphoblastic leukemia in adolescents and young adults', published 4 July 2026, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC13366240/, retrieved 2026-09-23
